sections.title: Habit and range
sections.text: Coronidium boormanii is an upright perennial herb 60–150 cm tall, known from hills north of Tenterfield in New South Wales, Australia. It grows in woodland and sclerophyll forest, often on shallow granite soils.

sections.title: Flower heads and plate
sections.text: Its flower heads are about 3–6 cm across. The plate shows narrow leaves, an upright stem and heads with pale bracts. Floral details are stylised and are not interpreted beyond the available evidence; no food use is established.
